options.text: First form the product: compute $5 \times 2 = 10$, then evaluate $6 + 10 - 4 = 12$.
Work strictly left to right as $((6+5)\times 2)-4$, as if brackets already fixed that order.
Call the answer multiplication only, without combining the remaining terms.
Also treat an exponent such as $2^{3}$ under the same left-to-right walk, as if this hinge settled powers.

stem:
Tanvi must evaluate the unbracketed expression $6 + 5 \times 2 - 4$.

Which order is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Without brackets, form the multiplication term first: 5×2=10, then 6+10-4=12. B pretends brackets force left-to-right. C stops at the word multiplication. D stretches the hinge to exponents.
